class PyMCSCMDGP(DGPMixin):
    """Plug a user-built PyMC causal model into badgers.

    Args:
        causal_model: a ``pm.Model`` following the module convention:
            structural nodes are named OBSERVED RVs listed in
            ``column_mapping``; their structural functions live in the
            distribution parameters; free RVs are Bayesian parameters.
        column_mapping: dict node name -> column index of the numpy
            data. Required (it NAMES the structural nodes).
        n_draws: posterior draws kept from ``pm.sample``.

    Requires the optional ``pymc`` extra (``pip install badgers[pymc]``).
    Latent free RVs must be continuous (PyMC's default NUTS step
    method); observed discrete nodes are supported.
    """

    def __init__(self, causal_model, column_mapping, n_draws=200):
        self._scm = causal_model
        self.column_mapping = dict(column_mapping)
        self.n_draws = int(n_draws)
        self._idata = None
        self._fns = {}        # node -> compiled param functions
        self._families = {}   # node -> (family name, param exprs)
        self._param_inputs = {}  # node -> fresh inputs per referenced RV
        self._pending = {}    # node -> params evaluated by the last
        # response call (draw_noise reuses them)
        self._free_names = None
        self._sampled = False
        self._derive_structure()

    # -- structure derivation ------------------------------------------------

    def _derive_structure(self):
        """Derive the DAG from the model's own graph BEFORE fitting.

        Uses the official ``pm.model_graph.model_to_networkx`` — its
        predecessors of a structural node include BOTH structural-node
        RVs (true causal parents) and parameter/free RVs (e.g. sigma);
        only the structural names are kept as parents. Structural RVs
        are exactly the ``column_mapping`` names; anything else must be
        a free RV (or a constant).
        """
        import pymc as pm

        structural = {}
        for name in self.column_mapping:
            rv = self._scm.named_vars.get(name)
            if rv is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Structural node '{name}' not found in the PyMC "
                    f"model's named variables."
                )
            structural[name] = rv

        graph = nx.DiGraph()
        graph.add_nodes_from(self.column_mapping)
        self._families = {}
        model_graph = pm.model_graph.model_to_networkx(self._scm)
        for name, rv in structural.items():
            if not rv.owner or rv.owner.inputs is None:
                raise ValueError(f"Node '{name}' is not a random variable.")
            family = type(rv.owner.op).__name__
            if family not in _ADDITIVE_FAMILIES and family not in _DISCRETE_FAMILIES:
                raise NotImplementedError(
                    f"PyMCSCMDGP does not support distribution family "
                    f"{family} for node '{name}' yet. Supported: "
                    f"{sorted(_ADDITIVE_FAMILIES) + list(_DISCRETE_FAMILIES)}."
                )
            # official graph: predecessors minus parameter RVs = parents
            parents = {
                pred for pred in model_graph.predecessors(name)
                if pred in structural and pred != name
            }
            for parent in sorted(parents):
                graph.add_edge(parent, name)
        self.graph = graph

    # -- fitting -------------------------------------------------------------

    def fit(self, X):
        """Validate the model, run ONE joint ``pm.sample``, compile the
        per-node parameter functions. NaN handling is delegated to the
        model the user wrote (complete-case policies are the user's
        PyMC modeling choice)."""
        import pymc as pm

        self._derive_structure()
        # validate observed-ness
        for name in self.column_mapping:
            observed_names = {v.name for v in self._scm.observed_RVs}
            if name not in observed_names:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Structural node '{name}' must be an observed RV "
                    f"(observed=<column>) — the joint posterior is "
                    f"identified through the observed data."
                )
        # compile + run the unsubstituted-RV safety scan BEFORE sampling:
        # validation errors must surface regardless of whether pm.sample
        # would even run (e.g. a model with no free RVs raises PyMC's
        # SamplingError before the scan could fire)
        self._compile_nodes()
        if self._scm.free_RVs:
            with self._scm:
                self._idata = pm.sample(
                    draws=self.n_draws,
                    tune=max(self.n_draws // 2, 100),
                    chains=1,
                    cores=1,
                    progressbar=False,
                    compute_convergence_checks=False,
                )
            self._free_names = [rv.name for rv in self._scm.free_RVs]
        else:
            # degenerate SCM: every structural function is a constant —
            # nothing to sample; the posterior draw index is a no-op
            self._free_names = []
        self._sampled = True
        return self

    def _compile_nodes(self):
        """Compile per-node parameter functions with shape-free inputs."""
        self._fns = {}
        self._param_inputs = {}
        for node in self.graph.nodes:
            rv = self._scm.named_vars[node]
            family = type(rv.owner.op).__name__
            params = list(rv.owner.inputs[2:])
            subst = {}
            # substitute every RV: parents (fresh per-node inputs) and
            # ALL free parameters (fresh inputs, one global input list)
            # The subst dict insertion order IS the compiled function
            # input order: parents (graph-predecessor order) first, then
            # free params in scm.free_RVs order — _eval relies on this.
            for parent in self.graph.predecessors(node):
                subst[self._scm.named_vars[parent]] = pt.vector(
                    f"{parent}__in_{node}", dtype="float64"
                )
            for free_rv in self._scm.free_RVs:
                if free_rv in subst:
                    continue
                subst[free_rv] = (
                    pt.vector(f"{free_rv.name}__in_{node}", dtype="float64")
                    if free_rv.owner.op.ndim_supp > 0
                    else pt.scalar(f"{free_rv.name}__in_{node}", dtype="float64")
                )
            memo = {}
            rebuilt = [_rebuild(e, subst, memo) for e in params]
            # safety scan on the REBUILT graph: a correct rebuild
            # substitutes EVERY RV with a plain vector/scalar input, so
            # no RV op may remain — any leftover is a freshly DRAWN RV
            # at evaluation (silent corruption — verified failure
            # mode). Map rebuilt RV copies back to the originals (via
            # the memo) to name the offender; references to non-parent
            # structural RVs land here.
            original_of = {
                new: orig for orig, new in memo.items()
                if new.owner and isinstance(new.owner.op, RandomVariable)
            }
            for expr in rebuilt:
                for anc in variable_ancestors([expr]):
                    if anc.owner and isinstance(
                        anc.owner.op, RandomVariable
                    ):
                        offender = original_of.get(anc, anc)
                        raise ValueError(
                            f"Node '{node}': its structural function "
                            f"references RV '{offender.name}' which is "
                            f"not one of its parents "
                            f"{[p for p in self.graph.predecessors(node)]} "
                            f"— unsubstituted RVs would be freshly drawn "
                            f"at evaluation (silent corruption)."
                        )
            inputs = list(subst.values())
            fns = [
                pytensor.function(inputs, expr, on_unused_input="ignore")
                for expr in rebuilt
            ]
            self._fns[node] = fns
            self._param_inputs[node] = inputs
            self._families[node] = (family, _ADDITIVE_FAMILIES.get(family))

    def is_fitted(self):
        """True iff the posterior is sampled and every node is compiled."""
        return (
            self._sampled
            and all(node in self._fns for node in self.graph.nodes)
        )

    def _posterior_flat(self, name):
        """(chains, draws, *shape) -> (chains*draws, *shape)."""
        values = np.asarray(self._idata.posterior[name].values)
        return values.reshape((-1,) + values.shape[2:])

    def _pinned_params(self, index):
        return {name: self._posterior_flat(name)[index]
                for name in self._free_names}

    def pick_parameters(self, rng=None):
        """Select ONE coherent posterior draw (from ``rng``) for this
        cascade; return a ``_ParameterDrawView``."""
        if self._free_names:
            total = self._posterior_flat(self._free_names[0]).shape[0]
        else:
            total = 1  # degenerate SCM: all parameters fixed constants
        return _ParameterDrawView(self, int(rng.integers(total)))

    # -- evaluation ----------------------------------------------------------

    def _eval(self, node, parent_values, pinned, which):
        fns = self._fns[node]
        inputs = self._param_inputs[node]
        args = []
        # inputs order: parents first, then free params — matching the
        # subst dict insertion order in _compile_nodes. parent_values
        # columns are in get_parents (== graph.predecessors) order.
        for col in range(parent_values.shape[1]):
            args.append(parent_values[:, col])
        for name in self._free_names:
            args.append(pinned[name])
        if which == "all":
            return [np.asarray(fn(*args)) for fn in fns]
        return np.asarray(fns[which](*args))

    def response(self, node, parent_values, pinned=None):
        pinned = pinned or self._pinned_params(0)
        family, roles = self._families[node]
        # evaluate ALL parameters once (they may depend on parents);
        # draw_noise reuses them via _pending — it takes no parents.
        params = self._eval(node, parent_values, pinned, "all")
        self._pending[node] = params
        if family in _DISCRETE_FAMILIES:
            # deterministic part contributes nothing: the VALUE comes
            # from draw_noise (whole-distribution draw)
            return np.zeros(parent_values.shape[0])
        loc = np.asarray(params[roles.index("mu")]).ravel()
        if loc.size == 1:
            loc = np.full(parent_values.shape[0], float(loc[0] if loc.shape else loc))
        return loc

    def draw_noise(self, node, rng, n, pinned=None):
        family, roles = self._families[node]
        if node not in self._pending:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"PyMCSCMDGP.draw_noise for node '{node}' requires a "
                f"preceding response(node, parent_values) call in the "
                f"same cascade"
            )
        params = self._pending.pop(node)  # set by the preceding response
        if family in _DISCRETE_FAMILIES:
            return self._draw_discrete(node, family, params, rng, n)
        # centered noise: loc already returned by response; the shape
        # parameter may be a scalar OR per-row (heteroscedastic)
        scale_idx = next(
            (roles.index(k) for k in ("sigma", "b") if k in roles), None
        )
        if scale_idx is not None:
            scale = np.broadcast_to(
                np.asarray(params[scale_idx], dtype=float).ravel(), (n,)
            )
        else:
            scale = 1.0
        if family == "NormalRV":
            return rng.normal(0.0, scale, size=n)
        if family == "StudentTRV":
            nu = np.asarray(params[roles.index("nu")], dtype=float).ravel()
            if nu.size not in (1, n):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Node '{node}': StudentT nu must be scalar or "
                    f"per-row (size {n}); got size {nu.size}"
                )
            return rng.standard_t(nu, size=n) * scale
        if family == "LaplaceRV":
            return rng.laplace(0.0, scale, size=n)
        raise NotImplementedError(f"No centered-noise rule for {family}")

    def _draw_discrete(self, node, family, params, rng, n):
        # per-row parameters must have shape (n,): a root node's scalar
        # (or (1,)-shaped) parameter would otherwise produce a single
        # draw broadcast to every row
        if family == "BernoulliRV":
            p = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(params[0], dtype=float).ravel(), (n,))
            return (rng.random(n) < p).astype(float)
        if family == "PoissonRV":
            mu = np.broadcast_to(
                np.asarray(params[0], dtype=float).ravel(), (n,)
            )
            return rng.poisson(np.maximum(mu, 1e-9)).astype(float)
        if family == "BinomialRV":
            n_trials = np.broadcast_to(
                np.asarray(params[0]).ravel(), (n,)
            )
            p = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(params[1], dtype=float).ravel(), (n,))
            return rng.binomial(n_trials.astype(int), p).astype(float)
        if family == "CategoricalRV":
            probs = np.asarray(params[0])
            probs = np.broadcast_to(probs, (n, probs.shape[-1]))
            u = rng.random(n)
            cum = np.cumsum(probs, axis=1)
            idx = (u[:, None] > cum).sum(axis=1)
            return np.clip(idx, 0, probs.shape[1] - 1).astype(float)
        raise NotImplementedError(f"No discrete draw rule for {family}")

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
Selectors: the observation-side contract for selecting deficit rows.

A SELECTOR decides which rows of the input get a data quality deficit:

Selector = Callable[[X, targets], dict[int, spec]]
  • keys = column positions (targets: the columns the mask applies to)
  • values = per-row boolean masks or float SCORES -- a (n,) array or, for Always-like constant levels, a scalar applied to the whole column
  • polarity: True/1.0 = R_X = 1 = deficit applied; False/0.0 = record as-is

A spec is a scalar or (n,) array of values in [0, 1]: values restricted to {0, 1} are DECISIONS, anything else is a PROBABILITY (the chance the deficit is applied to that row). Two rng streams cooperate: the PRESET's own rng drives the spec draw (the decision or probability computation, the stochastic row draws, the row weights), while the CONSUMER's rng drives the realization -- every spec is realized with the single rule rng.random(n) < spec. selector=None means no selector draw at all (the consumer decides). Being in core, the package is modality-agnostic: time-series / graph / text generators can reuse the same contract with masks over their own axes.

The presets are self-contained: their column scope (columns) and the column(s) they READ (bare int positions) are bound at construction, so an intensity sweep means constructing a new selector (nothing is swept on the call). There is deliberately no base class and no registry -- conformance to the :class:Selector protocol is defined by the call signature alone, and each preset's rule is inlined in __call__.

Exact-count presets (CountSelector, ClassCountSelector) bind a requested ROW count at construction -- the machinery behind the outliers generators' count knobs.

MODIFYING consumers preserve the input's shape and only ALTER the selected cells (missingness, noise, outliers, ...); SUBSAMPLING consumers (imbalance) DROP the selected rows, so their output is smaller than the input. The contract itself is only "which rows are selected, on which columns". All data used to determine selection, including class and driver columns, is supplied as X; there is no separate target argument.

Layout: :mod:.base holds the contract (protocol, shared validation, consumer helpers); :mod:.value_free and :mod:.value_driven hold the presets, split along the one constructor-contract difference they have (value-free presets never read X, value-driven presets read column positions).

class AlwaysSelector:
    """Selector: every row is selected, for every target column.

    The trivial, value- and rng-free rule -- the degenerate rule "apply
    the deficit everywhere". Emits the uniform spec ``1.0`` per target.

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers (its scope; call-time
        ``targets`` must stay inside it).
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int]):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        return {col: 1.0 for col in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"AlwaysSelector(columns={self.columns!r})"

class BernoulliSelector:
    """Selector: iid per-row, per-column deficit indicator draws.

    For each target column, whether a row is affected is an independent
    Bernoulli draw with probability ``rate``, independent of the data
    values. In the missingness literature this pattern is called
    "completely at random". One vectorized ``(n_rows, k)`` draw: column
    order follows ``targets`` order (RNG parity with the legacy
    per-variable draw order).

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    rate : float, in [0, 1]
        Per-cell selection probability.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], rate: float,
                 rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        self.rate = _validate_rate(rate, "rate")
        self.rng = rng

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        draws = self.rng.random(size=(X.shape[0], len(targets))) < self.rate
        return {col: draws[:, i] for i, col in enumerate(targets)}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"BernoulliSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"rate={self.rate!r})")

Selector: exactly counts[class_value] rows per listed class.

The value-driven exact-count preset (the class-aware sibling of :class:~badgers.core.selectors.value_free.CountSelector). Reads the class labels from class_column ONCE; for every class value in counts exactly that many rows of the class are drawn WITHOUT REPLACEMENT (uniform) and the union mask is returned under every target. Classes absent from counts select nothing; a count for a class value missing from X raises (typo protection), and a count above the class size raises (an explicit count is a request, not a share -- unlike :class:ClassSelector's share clipping).

    target. Classes absent from ``counts`` select nothing; a count for a
    class value missing from ``X`` raises (typo protection), and a count
    above the class size raises (an explicit count is a request, not a
    share -- unlike :class:`ClassSelector`'s share clipping).

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    class_column : int
        Position of the column holding the class labels.
    counts : dict mapping class_value -> int
        Exact number of rows selected per class value (ints >= 0).
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the row draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], class_column: int,
                 counts: dict, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(class_column, (int, np.integer)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"class_column must be an int position, got {class_column!r}")
        self.class_column = int(class_column)
        for value, count in counts.items():
            if not isinstance(count, (int, np.integer)) or isinstance(count, bool):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"counts[{value!r}] must be an int, got {count!r}")
            if count < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"counts[{value!r}] must be >= 0, got {count}")
        self.counts = counts
        self.rng = rng

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        n_rows = X.shape[0]
        labels = X[:, self.class_column]
        values = set(np.unique(labels).tolist())
        unknown = [v for v in self.counts if v not in values]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"class value(s) {unknown!r} not found in column "
                f"{self.class_column} (found {sorted(values)!r})")
        mask = np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=bool)
        for class_value, count in self.counts.items():
            rows = np.flatnonzero(labels == class_value)
            if count > len(rows):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"counts[{class_value!r}]={count} exceeds the number "
                    f"of rows of class {class_value!r} ({len(rows)})")
            if count:
                # Sampling without replacement: sequential by nature.
                idx = self.rng.choice(rows, size=count, replace=False)
                mask[idx] = True
        return {t: mask for t in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"ClassCountSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"class_column={self.class_column!r}, "
                f"counts={self.counts!r})")

class ClassSelector:
    """Selector: selects a fixed share of the rows of each listed class.

    Reads the class labels from ``class_column`` ONCE; for every class
    value in ``proportions`` exactly ``min(int(share * n_rows),
    n_rows_in_class)`` rows of that class are drawn WITHOUT REPLACEMENT
    (uniform). The class values are discovered from ``X``; a proportion
    for an absent class raises ``ValueError`` (typo protection). The
    resulting mask is returned under EVERY target column (one read,
    broadcast across targets).

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    class_column : int
        Position of the column holding the class labels.
    proportions : dict mapping class_value -> float in [0, 1]
        Share of the TOTAL row count selected per class value.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], class_column: int,
                 proportions: dict, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(class_column, (int, np.integer)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"class_column must be an int position, got {class_column!r}")
        self.class_column = int(class_column)
        for value, share in proportions.items():
            _validate_rate(share, f"proportions[{value!r}]")
        self.proportions = proportions
        self.rng = rng

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        if not (0 <= self.class_column < X.shape[1]):
            raise ValueError(
                f"the selector's class_column {self.class_column} is not a "
                f"valid column position in X with {X.shape[1]} columns")
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        n_rows = X.shape[0]
        col = X[:, self.class_column]
        values = set(np.unique(col).tolist())
        unknown = [v for v in self.proportions if v not in values]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"class value(s) {unknown!r} not found in column "
                f"{self.class_column} (found {sorted(values)!r})")
        mask = np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=bool)
        for class_value, share in self.proportions.items():
            rows = np.flatnonzero(col == class_value)
            # Share of the TOTAL row count, clipped to the class size.
            count = min(int(share * n_rows), len(rows))
            if count:
                # Sampling without replacement: sequential by nature.
                idx = self.rng.choice(rows, size=count, replace=False)
                mask[idx] = True
        return {col: mask for col in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"ClassSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"class_column={self.class_column!r}, "
                f"proportions={self.proportions!r})")

class CountSelector:
    """Selector: exactly ``count`` distinct rows, one shared mask.

    The exact-count ROW preset: draws ``count`` row positions without
    replacement (uniform) and returns the same boolean mask under every
    target column — the requested count is exact at ROW level. This is
    the machinery behind the outliers generators' default count: an
    explicit count is a request, and a request that overflows the data
    raises.

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    count : int
        Number of rows to select; must be an int >= 0 and <= the number
        of rows of the ``X`` passed at call time.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the row draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], count: int,
                 rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(count, (int, np.integer)) or isinstance(count, bool):
            raise ValueError(f"count must be an int, got {count!r}")
        if count < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"count must be >= 0, got {count}")
        self.count = int(count)
        self.rng = rng

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        n_rows = X.shape[0]
        if self.count > n_rows:
            raise ValueError(
                f"count {self.count} exceeds the number of rows of X "
                f"({n_rows}): an exact count cannot select more distinct "
                "rows than exist")
        if self.count == 0:
            empty = np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=bool)
            return {col: empty for col in targets}
        # Sampling without replacement: sequential by nature.
        idx = self.rng.choice(n_rows, size=self.count, replace=False)
        mask = _mask_from_indices(n_rows, idx)
        return {col: mask for col in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"CountSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"count={self.count!r})")

class ExactCountSelector:
    """Selector: exactly ``int(rate * n_rows)`` rows per target column,
    drawn without replacement (uniform, or weighted by per-row
    probabilities).

    The exact-count sibling of :class:`BernoulliSelector`. Per column, a
    fixed number of affected rows, optionally with per-row selection
    probabilities ("soft" coupling).

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    rate : float, in [0, 1]
        Affected rows per column = ``int(rate * n_rows)`` (floor).
    weights : None, (n_rows, k) array, or callable ``(X) -> (n_rows, k)``
        Per-row selection probabilities, one column per target.
        ``None`` = uniform. The callable is evaluated per call (the
        caller binds any randomness inside it, BEFORE the row draws).
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], rate: float,
                 weights: np.ndarray
                 | Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray] | None = None,
                 rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        self.rate = _validate_rate(rate, "rate")
        self.weights = weights
        self.rng = rng

    def _resolve_weights(self, X: np.ndarray, targets) -> np.ndarray | None:
        k = len(targets)
        if self.weights is None:
            return None
        w = self.weights(X) if callable(self.weights) else self.weights
        w = np.asarray(w, dtype=float)
        if w.shape != (X.shape[0], k):
            raise ValueError(
                f"weights must have shape ({X.shape[0]}, {k}), got {w.shape}")
        if (w < 0).any():
            raise ValueError("weights must be non-negative")
        return w

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        n_rows = X.shape[0]
        count = int(self.rate * n_rows)
        # Resolve the weights BEFORE the row draws: data-driven coupling
        # may consume rng draws itself, and those must precede the per-
        # column row draws (draw-order parity with the classic generators).
        weights = self._resolve_weights(X, targets)
        masks = {}
        for i, col in enumerate(targets):
            # Sampling without replacement: sequential by nature.
            p = None if weights is None else weights[:, i]
            if count == n_rows and p is not None:
                # The whole population is requested: the draw is forced
                # regardless of the weights (numpy rejects rows whose
                # weight is exactly 0 in that case) -- bypass the sampler.
                idx = np.arange(n_rows)
            else:
                idx = self.rng.choice(n_rows, size=count, replace=False, p=p)
            masks[col] = _mask_from_indices(n_rows, idx)
        return masks

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"ExactCountSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"rate={self.rate!r})")

class ProportionalSelector:
    """Selector: the deficit probability is proportional to a column's value.

    Value-driven, FRACTIONAL rule: the per-row score is the min-max
    normalized value of ``column`` rescaled to sum to 1 (a constant
    column yields the uniform score). Deterministic (no rng); the
    consumer decides how the probabilities are realized.

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    column : int
        Position of the column whose values drive the scores.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], column: int):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(column, (int, np.integer)):
            raise ValueError(f"column must be an int position, got {column!r}")
        self.column = int(column)

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        col = X[:, self.column].astype(float)
        span = col.max() - col.min()
        unit = (col - col.min()) / span if span > 0 else np.ones_like(col)
        scores = normalize_proba(unit)
        return {c: scores for c in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"ProportionalSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"column={self.column!r})")

class TopQuantileSelector:
    """Selector: selects rows where the column value is >= its quantile.

    Deterministic rule: threshold = ``np.quantile(X[:, driver], quantile)``
    (``driver=None``: the column's own threshold). A row is selected when the
    driver value is ``>= threshold``; the same mask is returned under
    every target.

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    column : int
        Required read column; unused when ``driver`` is set. In self
        mode (``driver=None``) the threshold is compared against this
        column (``column == driver``).
    quantile : float, in [0, 1]
        The quantile forming the threshold (``>=`` comparison).
    driver : int or None, default=None
        Driver column position whose values form the threshold and mask.
        ``None`` = self mode (driver is ``column``).
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], column: int,
                 quantile: float, driver: int | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(column, (int, np.integer)):
            raise ValueError(f"column must be an int position, got {column!r}")
        self.column = int(column)
        self.driver = self.column if driver is None else int(driver)
        self.quantile = _validate_rate(quantile, "quantile")

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        dcol = X[:, self.driver]
        threshold = np.quantile(dcol, self.quantile)
        mask = dcol >= threshold
        return {col: mask for col in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"TopQuantileSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"column={self.column!r}, quantile={self.quantile!r}, "
                f"driver={self.driver!r})")

Column i corresponds to the selector's i-th target (its own columns when it declares a scope, else every column). Narrow on purpose: the caller decides how to write the field back into full coordinates.

def get_selected_fields(X, selector, rng):
    """Realized selection field: bool array ``(n_rows, len(targets))``.

    Column *i* corresponds to the selector's *i*-th target (its own
    ``columns`` when it declares a scope, else every column). Narrow on
    purpose: the caller decides how to write the field back into full
    coordinates.

    ``selector=None`` returns every column all-True WITHOUT consuming rng
    draws — the backward-compatible default of consuming generators.

    Single realization rule (shared with every consumer):
    ``rng.random(n) < spec``; the mask is decided against the UN-mutated
    input. Constant decisions (a scalar spec of exactly ``0.0`` or
    ``1.0``) are deterministic and realized WITHOUT consuming rng draws,
    so default selectors built on ``AlwaysSelector`` cost no draws.
    """
    n_rows, n_cols = X.shape
    if selector is None:
        return np.ones((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)
    targets = _resolve_targets(selector, X, None)
    out = selector(X, targets=list(targets))
    unknown = [c for c in out if c not in targets]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"selector returned keys {unknown} not in targets {targets}")
    field = np.zeros((n_rows, len(targets)), dtype=bool)
    for i, col in enumerate(targets):
        if col in out:
            spec = out[col]
            _check_spec(spec, n_rows)
            spec = np.asarray(spec)
            if spec.ndim == 0 and float(spec) in (0.0, 1.0):
                # constant decision: deterministic, no rng draw consumed
                field[:, i] = float(spec)
            else:
                field[:, i] = rng.random(n_rows) < np.broadcast_to(spec, (n_rows,))
    return field

def resolve_class_column(selector, X: np.ndarray):
    """Recover the class column position from a value-reading selector.

    Value-driven presets expose a ``class_column`` (or ``column``)
    attribute holding the read column position. Returns ``None`` when the
    selector has no such attribute or the value is out of range.
    """
    col = getattr(selector, "class_column", None)
    if col is None:
        col = getattr(selector, "column", None)
    if col is not None and 0 <= col < X.shape[1]:
        return col
    return None

Value-driven selector presets: rules that read column values.

These presets READ values from X, so they are constructed with the read column position(s) as bare ints. The column positions they COVER (columns) are their scope: the returned dict has one key per target.

docs.title: ClassCountSelector
docs.text:
Selector: exactly counts[class_value] rows per listed class.

The value-driven exact-count preset (the class-aware sibling of :class:~badgers.core.selectors.value_free.CountSelector). Reads the class labels from class_column ONCE; for every class value in counts exactly that many rows of the class are drawn WITHOUT REPLACEMENT (uniform) and the union mask is returned under every target. Classes absent from counts select nothing; a count for a class value missing from X raises (typo protection), and a count above the class size raises (an explicit count is a request, not a share -- unlike :class:ClassSelector's share clipping).

class ClassCountSelector:
    """Selector: exactly ``counts[class_value]`` rows per listed class.

    The value-driven exact-count preset (the class-aware sibling of
    :class:`~badgers.core.selectors.value_free.CountSelector`). Reads the
    class labels from ``class_column`` ONCE; for every class value in
    ``counts`` exactly that many rows of the class are drawn WITHOUT
    REPLACEMENT (uniform) and the union mask is returned under every
    target. Classes absent from ``counts`` select nothing; a count for a
    class value missing from ``X`` raises (typo protection), and a count
    above the class size raises (an explicit count is a request, not a
    share -- unlike :class:`ClassSelector`'s share clipping).

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    class_column : int
        Position of the column holding the class labels.
    counts : dict mapping class_value -> int
        Exact number of rows selected per class value (ints >= 0).
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the row draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], class_column: int,
                 counts: dict, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(class_column, (int, np.integer)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"class_column must be an int position, got {class_column!r}")
        self.class_column = int(class_column)
        for value, count in counts.items():
            if not isinstance(count, (int, np.integer)) or isinstance(count, bool):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"counts[{value!r}] must be an int, got {count!r}")
            if count < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"counts[{value!r}] must be >= 0, got {count}")
        self.counts = counts
        self.rng = rng

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        n_rows = X.shape[0]
        labels = X[:, self.class_column]
        values = set(np.unique(labels).tolist())
        unknown = [v for v in self.counts if v not in values]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"class value(s) {unknown!r} not found in column "
                f"{self.class_column} (found {sorted(values)!r})")
        mask = np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=bool)
        for class_value, count in self.counts.items():
            rows = np.flatnonzero(labels == class_value)
            if count > len(rows):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"counts[{class_value!r}]={count} exceeds the number "
                    f"of rows of class {class_value!r} ({len(rows)})")
            if count:
                # Sampling without replacement: sequential by nature.
                idx = self.rng.choice(rows, size=count, replace=False)
                mask[idx] = True
        return {t: mask for t in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"ClassCountSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"class_column={self.class_column!r}, "
                f"counts={self.counts!r})")

docs.text:
Selector: selects a fixed share of the rows of each listed class.

Reads the class labels from class_column ONCE; for every class value in proportions exactly min(int(share * n_rows), n_rows_in_class) rows of that class are drawn WITHOUT REPLACEMENT (uniform). The class values are discovered from X; a proportion for an absent class raises ValueError (typo protection). The resulting mask is returned under EVERY target column (one read, broadcast across targets).

class ClassSelector:
    """Selector: selects a fixed share of the rows of each listed class.

    Reads the class labels from ``class_column`` ONCE; for every class
    value in ``proportions`` exactly ``min(int(share * n_rows),
    n_rows_in_class)`` rows of that class are drawn WITHOUT REPLACEMENT
    (uniform). The class values are discovered from ``X``; a proportion
    for an absent class raises ``ValueError`` (typo protection). The
    resulting mask is returned under EVERY target column (one read,
    broadcast across targets).

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    class_column : int
        Position of the column holding the class labels.
    proportions : dict mapping class_value -> float in [0, 1]
        Share of the TOTAL row count selected per class value.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], class_column: int,
                 proportions: dict, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(class_column, (int, np.integer)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"class_column must be an int position, got {class_column!r}")
        self.class_column = int(class_column)
        for value, share in proportions.items():
            _validate_rate(share, f"proportions[{value!r}]")
        self.proportions = proportions
        self.rng = rng

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        if not (0 <= self.class_column < X.shape[1]):
            raise ValueError(
                f"the selector's class_column {self.class_column} is not a "
                f"valid column position in X with {X.shape[1]} columns")
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        n_rows = X.shape[0]
        col = X[:, self.class_column]
        values = set(np.unique(col).tolist())
        unknown = [v for v in self.proportions if v not in values]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"class value(s) {unknown!r} not found in column "
                f"{self.class_column} (found {sorted(values)!r})")
        mask = np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=bool)
        for class_value, share in self.proportions.items():
            rows = np.flatnonzero(col == class_value)
            # Share of the TOTAL row count, clipped to the class size.
            count = min(int(share * n_rows), len(rows))
            if count:
                # Sampling without replacement: sequential by nature.
                idx = self.rng.choice(rows, size=count, replace=False)
                mask[idx] = True
        return {col: mask for col in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"ClassSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"class_column={self.class_column!r}, "
                f"proportions={self.proportions!r})")

Selector: the deficit probability is proportional to a column's value.

Value-driven, FRACTIONAL rule: the per-row score is the min-max normalized value of column rescaled to sum to 1 (a constant column yields the uniform score). Deterministic (no rng); the consumer decides how the probabilities are realized.

class ProportionalSelector:
    """Selector: the deficit probability is proportional to a column's value.

    Value-driven, FRACTIONAL rule: the per-row score is the min-max
    normalized value of ``column`` rescaled to sum to 1 (a constant
    column yields the uniform score). Deterministic (no rng); the
    consumer decides how the probabilities are realized.

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    column : int
        Position of the column whose values drive the scores.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], column: int):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(column, (int, np.integer)):
            raise ValueError(f"column must be an int position, got {column!r}")
        self.column = int(column)

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        col = X[:, self.column].astype(float)
        span = col.max() - col.min()
        unit = (col - col.min()) / span if span > 0 else np.ones_like(col)
        scores = normalize_proba(unit)
        return {c: scores for c in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"ProportionalSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"column={self.column!r})")

class TopQuantileSelector:
    """Selector: selects rows where the column value is >= its quantile.

    Deterministic rule: threshold = ``np.quantile(X[:, driver], quantile)``
    (``driver=None``: the column's own threshold). A row is selected when the
    driver value is ``>= threshold``; the same mask is returned under
    every target.

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    column : int
        Required read column; unused when ``driver`` is set. In self
        mode (``driver=None``) the threshold is compared against this
        column (``column == driver``).
    quantile : float, in [0, 1]
        The quantile forming the threshold (``>=`` comparison).
    driver : int or None, default=None
        Driver column position whose values form the threshold and mask.
        ``None`` = self mode (driver is ``column``).
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], column: int,
                 quantile: float, driver: int | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(column, (int, np.integer)):
            raise ValueError(f"column must be an int position, got {column!r}")
        self.column = int(column)
        self.driver = self.column if driver is None else int(driver)
        self.quantile = _validate_rate(quantile, "quantile")

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        dcol = X[:, self.driver]
        threshold = np.quantile(dcol, self.quantile)
        mask = dcol >= threshold
        return {col: mask for col in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"TopQuantileSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"column={self.column!r}, quantile={self.quantile!r}, "
                f"driver={self.driver!r})")

docs.title: value_free
docs.text:
Value-free selector presets: rules that never read column values.

Because the rule is value-blind, no read column is needed at construction; the presets take columns (the column positions they cover). Two rng streams: the preset's own rng draws the mask (bind it at construction with rng=; a stochastic preset without one raises), while the consuming generator realizes the returned masks with its own rng (rng.random(n) < spec). Some consumers instead hand their own rng to the preset at construction (e.g. the missingness generators build ExactCountSelector(..., rng=...) from their stream) -- the preset's draw is then the consumer's stream.

class AlwaysSelector:
    """Selector: every row is selected, for every target column.

    The trivial, value- and rng-free rule -- the degenerate rule "apply
    the deficit everywhere". Emits the uniform spec ``1.0`` per target.

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers (its scope; call-time
        ``targets`` must stay inside it).
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int]):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        return {col: 1.0 for col in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"AlwaysSelector(columns={self.columns!r})"

docs.title: BernoulliSelector
docs.text:
Selector: iid per-row, per-column deficit indicator draws.

For each target column, whether a row is affected is an independent Bernoulli draw with probability rate, independent of the data values. In the missingness literature this pattern is called "completely at random". One vectorized (n_rows, k) draw: column order follows targets order (RNG parity with the legacy per-variable draw order).

class BernoulliSelector:
    """Selector: iid per-row, per-column deficit indicator draws.

    For each target column, whether a row is affected is an independent
    Bernoulli draw with probability ``rate``, independent of the data
    values. In the missingness literature this pattern is called
    "completely at random". One vectorized ``(n_rows, k)`` draw: column
    order follows ``targets`` order (RNG parity with the legacy
    per-variable draw order).

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    rate : float, in [0, 1]
        Per-cell selection probability.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], rate: float,
                 rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        self.rate = _validate_rate(rate, "rate")
        self.rng = rng

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        draws = self.rng.random(size=(X.shape[0], len(targets))) < self.rate
        return {col: draws[:, i] for i, col in enumerate(targets)}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"BernoulliSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"rate={self.rate!r})")

The exact-count ROW preset: draws count row positions without replacement (uniform) and returns the same boolean mask under every target column — the requested count is exact at ROW level. This is the machinery behind the outliers generators' default count: an explicit count is a request, and a request that overflows the data raises.

class CountSelector:
    """Selector: exactly ``count`` distinct rows, one shared mask.

    The exact-count ROW preset: draws ``count`` row positions without
    replacement (uniform) and returns the same boolean mask under every
    target column — the requested count is exact at ROW level. This is
    the machinery behind the outliers generators' default count: an
    explicit count is a request, and a request that overflows the data
    raises.

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    count : int
        Number of rows to select; must be an int >= 0 and <= the number
        of rows of the ``X`` passed at call time.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the row draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], count: int,
                 rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        if not isinstance(count, (int, np.integer)) or isinstance(count, bool):
            raise ValueError(f"count must be an int, got {count!r}")
        if count < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"count must be >= 0, got {count}")
        self.count = int(count)
        self.rng = rng

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        n_rows = X.shape[0]
        if self.count > n_rows:
            raise ValueError(
                f"count {self.count} exceeds the number of rows of X "
                f"({n_rows}): an exact count cannot select more distinct "
                "rows than exist")
        if self.count == 0:
            empty = np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=bool)
            return {col: empty for col in targets}
        # Sampling without replacement: sequential by nature.
        idx = self.rng.choice(n_rows, size=self.count, replace=False)
        mask = _mask_from_indices(n_rows, idx)
        return {col: mask for col in targets}

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"CountSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"count={self.count!r})")

class ExactCountSelector:
    """Selector: exactly ``int(rate * n_rows)`` rows per target column,
    drawn without replacement (uniform, or weighted by per-row
    probabilities).

    The exact-count sibling of :class:`BernoulliSelector`. Per column, a
    fixed number of affected rows, optionally with per-row selection
    probabilities ("soft" coupling).

    Parameters
    ----------
    columns : int or sequence of int
        Column positions this selector covers.
    rate : float, in [0, 1]
        Affected rows per column = ``int(rate * n_rows)`` (floor).
    weights : None, (n_rows, k) array, or callable ``(X) -> (n_rows, k)``
        Per-row selection probabilities, one column per target.
        ``None`` = uniform. The callable is evaluated per call (the
        caller binds any randomness inside it, BEFORE the row draws).
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator used for the draws.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int | Sequence[int], rate: float,
                 weights: np.ndarray
                 | Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray] | None = None,
                 rng: np.random.Generator | None = None):
        self.columns = _validate_columns(columns)
        self.rate = _validate_rate(rate, "rate")
        self.weights = weights
        self.rng = rng

    def _resolve_weights(self, X: np.ndarray, targets) -> np.ndarray | None:
        k = len(targets)
        if self.weights is None:
            return None
        w = self.weights(X) if callable(self.weights) else self.weights
        w = np.asarray(w, dtype=float)
        if w.shape != (X.shape[0], k):
            raise ValueError(
                f"weights must have shape ({X.shape[0]}, {k}), got {w.shape}")
        if (w < 0).any():
            raise ValueError("weights must be non-negative")
        return w

    def __call__(self, X: np.ndarray, targets=None):
        _require_rng(self)
        targets = _resolve_targets(self, X, targets)
        n_rows = X.shape[0]
        count = int(self.rate * n_rows)
        # Resolve the weights BEFORE the row draws: data-driven coupling
        # may consume rng draws itself, and those must precede the per-
        # column row draws (draw-order parity with the classic generators).
        weights = self._resolve_weights(X, targets)
        masks = {}
        for i, col in enumerate(targets):
            # Sampling without replacement: sequential by nature.
            p = None if weights is None else weights[:, i]
            if count == n_rows and p is not None:
                # The whole population is requested: the draw is forced
                # regardless of the weights (numpy rejects rows whose
                # weight is exactly 0 in that case) -- bypass the sampler.
                idx = np.arange(n_rows)
            else:
                idx = self.rng.choice(n_rows, size=count, replace=False, p=p)
            masks[col] = _mask_from_indices(n_rows, idx)
        return masks

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"ExactCountSelector(columns={self.columns!r}, "
                f"rate={self.rate!r})")

class EdgesMissingCompletelyAtRandom(MissingGenerator):
    """
    Removes edges from the graph uniformly at random.
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator):
        """
        Initialize the missingness generator.

        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator.
                                 Required (no default): pass a numpy.random.Generator.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        super().__init__(random_generator=random_generator)

    def generate(self, X, percentage_missing: float = 0.1):
        """
        Generate a graph with a specified percentage of missing edges.

        Any values associated with the edges (e.g., edge attributes such as weights)
        are stored as attributes on the graph edges themselves. When an edge is removed,
        its associated values are removed with it.

        :param X: The input graph from which edges will be removed.
        :type X: nx.Graph
        :param percentage_missing: The percentage of edges to be removed (float value between 0 and 1).
        :type percentage_missing: float
        :return: The modified graph with missing edges.
        :rtype: nx.Graph
        """
        if not 0 < percentage_missing < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"percentage_missing must be in (0, 1), got {percentage_missing}")
        if not isinstance(X, nx.Graph):
            raise TypeError('badgers does only support networkx.Graph objects for graphs')

        edges_to_be_removed = self.random_generator.choice(
            X.edges(),
            int(X.number_of_edges() * percentage_missing),
            replace=False
        )

        Xt = X.copy()
        Xt.remove_edges_from(edges_to_be_removed)

        return Xt

def generate(self, X, percentage_missing: float = 0.1):
    """
    Generate a graph with a specified percentage of missing edges.

    Any values associated with the edges (e.g., edge attributes such as weights)
    are stored as attributes on the graph edges themselves. When an edge is removed,
    its associated values are removed with it.

    :param X: The input graph from which edges will be removed.
    :type X: nx.Graph
    :param percentage_missing: The percentage of edges to be removed (float value between 0 and 1).
    :type percentage_missing: float
    :return: The modified graph with missing edges.
    :rtype: nx.Graph
    """
    if not 0 < percentage_missing < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"percentage_missing must be in (0, 1), got {percentage_missing}")
    if not isinstance(X, nx.Graph):
        raise TypeError('badgers does only support networkx.Graph objects for graphs')

    edges_to_be_removed = self.random_generator.choice(
        X.edges(),
        int(X.number_of_edges() * percentage_missing),
        replace=False
    )

    Xt = X.copy()
    Xt.remove_edges_from(edges_to_be_removed)

    return Xt

class NodesMissingCompletelyAtRandom(MissingGenerator):
    """
    Removes nodes from the graph uniformly at random.
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator):
        """
        Initialize the missingness generator.

        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator.
                               Required (no default): pass a numpy.random.Generator.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        super().__init__(random_generator=random_generator)

    def generate(self, X, percentage_missing: float = 0.1):
        """
        Generate a graph with a specified percentage of missing nodes.

        Any values associated with the nodes (e.g., node attributes such as labels)
        are stored as attributes on the graph nodes themselves. When a node is removed,
        its associated values are removed with it.

        :param X: The input graph from which nodes will be removed.
        :type X: nx.Graph
        :param percentage_missing: The percentage of nodes to be removed (float value between 0 and 1).
        :type percentage_missing: float
        :return: The modified graph with missing nodes.
        :rtype: nx.Graph
        """
        if not 0 < percentage_missing < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"percentage_missing must be in (0, 1), got {percentage_missing}")
        if not isinstance(X, nx.Graph):
            raise TypeError('badgers does only support networkx.Graph objects for graphs')

        nodes_to_be_removed = self.random_generator.choice(
            X.nodes(),
            int(X.number_of_nodes() * percentage_missing),
            replace=False
        )

        Xt = X.copy()
        Xt.remove_nodes_from(nodes_to_be_removed)

        return Xt

docs.text:
Causal data quality defect generators.

The causal defect family generates bad data by perturbing the structure (causal graph + data generation process) of the data, rather than the raw values. Each generator fits a per-node DGP to the data (the default OLS backend is pure NumPy and needs no extra dependencies), applies a structural perturbation, then propagates the effect through the descendants.

Custom estimation backends (e.g. PyMC- or DoWhy-GCM-based) can be provided via the dgp argument of fit; the optional pymc / dowhy extras are only needed for using those backends::

pip install "badgers[pymc]"    # PyMC-based backend
pip install "badgers[dowhy]"   # DoWhy-GCM-based backend

def __getattr__(name):
    """Resolve generator names on first access (lazy import)."""
    module_name = _LAZY_ATTRS.get(name)
    if module_name is None:
        raise AttributeError(
            f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}"
        )
    import importlib

    module = importlib.import_module(module_name)
    return getattr(module, name)

docs.title: _base
docs.text:
Shared base class for the causal data quality defect generators.

Owns the shared plumbing: DGP configuration (no generator-side fit — the DGP is fitted by its own fit, explicitly by the caller or lazily inside generate()) and input/structure validation. Subclasses define the defect injection and propagation, and manage their OWN labels: each generator stores the per-row defect labels of its last generated output and exposes them through a public getter (e.g. get_outliers_labels()).

Selection (which rows get the defect) is realized by badgers.core.selectors.get_selected_fields; generators import and call it themselves. The DGP's column_mapping is the ONLY name↔position bridge: generators speak column positions, and _node_names translates them back at the intervene boundary.

No generator-side fit, no graph-only configuration Causal generators have NO public fit() — the only fitted object is the DGP (DGP.fit), consistent with the rest of the library. The DGP is fitted either EXPLICITLY by the caller (preferred) or lazily INSIDE generate() when the configured DGP is still unfitted (_require_dgp).

Pipelines In a pipeline, each causal stage receives the PREVIOUS stage's output as input. Fitting the DGP lazily on that contaminated input would refit the world per stage (and, with NaN-bearing columns, trigger complete-case filtering). Fit the DGP ONCE on the clean entry data and share the fitted instance::

    dgp = GcmSCMDGP(make_gcm_scm(graph, column_mapping)).fit(X)  # fit on clean X

    missingness = CausalMissingnessGenerator(random_generator=..., dgp=dgp)
    Xm = missingness.generate(X, ...)

    drift = CausalDriftGenerator(random_generator=..., dgp=dgp)  # share
    Xt = drift.generate(Xm, ...)

All per-stage scale computations are NaN-safe, so even the lazy
refit path behaves sensibly; the explicitly-fitted shared
``dgp=`` pattern simply guarantees ONE world for the whole
pipeline. Fit the DGP once on clean data — the backends do not
impute or filter NaN rows at fit time.

class CausalGenerator(GeneratorMixin):
    """Base class for causal defect generators.

    Parameters
    ----------
    random_generator : numpy.random.Generator, required
        Random number generator instance.
    dgp : DGP or None, default=None
        DGP instance (fitted or unfitted). This is the ONLY structure
        the generator accepts — a DGP carries its own graph and
        column_mapping. There is no graph-only configuration and no
        implicit default backend: if ``dgp`` is None, ``generate()``
        raises (build one with e.g.
        ``GcmSCMDGP(make_gcm_scm(graph, column_mapping))``).

    Notes
    -----
    No generator-side ``fit``, no graph-only configuration
        Causal generators have NO public ``fit()`` — the only fitted
        object is the DGP (``DGP.fit``), consistent with the rest of the
        library. The DGP is fitted either EXPLICITLY by the caller
        (preferred) or lazily INSIDE ``generate()`` when the configured
        DGP is still unfitted (``_require_dgp``).

    Pipelines
        In a pipeline, each causal stage receives the PREVIOUS stage's
        output as input. Fitting the DGP lazily on that contaminated
        input would refit the world per stage (and, with NaN-bearing
        columns, trigger complete-case filtering). Fit the DGP ONCE on
        the clean entry data and share the fitted instance::

            dgp = GcmSCMDGP(make_gcm_scm(graph, column_mapping)).fit(X)  # fit on clean X

            missingness = CausalMissingnessGenerator(random_generator=..., dgp=dgp)
            Xm = missingness.generate(X, ...)

            drift = CausalDriftGenerator(random_generator=..., dgp=dgp)  # share
            Xt = drift.generate(Xm, ...)

        All per-stage scale computations are NaN-safe, so even the lazy
        refit path behaves sensibly; the explicitly-fitted shared
        ``dgp=`` pattern simply guarantees ONE world for the whole
        pipeline. Fit the DGP once on clean data — the backends do not
        impute or filter NaN rows at fit time.
    """

    #: Subclasses set this to the deficit name used in labels.
    deficit_name = "causal"

    def __init__(self, random_generator, dgp=None):
        self.random_generator = random_generator
        self.dgp = dgp
        self.graph = None if dgp is None else dgp.graph
        self.column_mapping = None if dgp is None else dgp.column_mapping
        # Per-row deficit labels of the last generated output. Subclasses
        # fill this in ``generate()`` and expose it through their own
        # public getter (e.g. ``get_outliers_labels()``) which raises
        # RuntimeError when no output has been generated yet.
        self.deficit_labels_ = None

    def _get_deficit_labels(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Shared body of the per-family ``get_<deficit>_labels()`` getters.

        Returns ``self.deficit_labels_`` (the boolean per-row field filled
        by ``generate()``); raises ``RuntimeError`` when no output has
        been generated yet. The error message names the family through
        ``self.deficit_name``.
        """
        if self.deficit_labels_ is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"{self.deficit_name.capitalize()} labels are only "
                "available after calling generate()."
            )
        return self.deficit_labels_

    # -- DGP plumbing -------------------------------------------------------

    def use_dgp(self, dgp):
        """Attach a DGP (fitted or unfitted); the structure comes with it.

        An unfitted DGP is fitted lazily inside ``generate()`` on the
        generate-time data (``_require_dgp``). Prefer attaching a DGP you
        fitted explicitly on the clean entry data (shared across a
        pipeline).
        """
        self.dgp = dgp
        self.graph = dgp.graph
        self.column_mapping = dgp.column_mapping

    def _require_fitted(self):
        if self.graph is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Generator has no structure: pass a dgp=... to the "
                "constructor, or use use_dgp(dgp), before generate()."
            )

    def _require_dgp(self, X=None):
        """Require a fitted DGP; fit lazily on demand.

        Call ``_require_dgp(X)`` before any column mutation so the DGP is
        fitted on the ORIGINAL data. Two routes:

        1. a fitted DGP was configured/attached — nothing to do;
        2. an UNFITTED DGP was configured/attached — it is fitted here
           on ``X`` (the generate-time data).

        There is NO implicit default backend: if no DGP was given,
        ``generate()`` fails. Build the world explicitly, e.g.
        ``dgp = GcmSCMDGP(make_gcm_scm(graph, column_mapping)).fit(X)``.
        """
        if self.dgp is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "This generator needs a DGP: pass a dgp=... to the "
                "constructor, or use use_dgp(dgp), before generate(). "
                "Build one with e.g. dgp = GcmSCMDGP(make_gcm_scm("
                "graph, column_mapping)).fit(X)."
            )
        elif not self.dgp.is_fitted():
            self.dgp.fit(X)

    def _sample(self, n_samples):
        """Delegate sampling to the fitted DGP."""
        if self.dgp is None or not self.dgp.is_fitted():
            raise RuntimeError(
                "_sample requires a fitted DGP: pass a fitted dgp=... to "
                "the constructor (or use_dgp(dgp)) first."
            )
        return self.dgp.sample(self.random_generator, n_samples)

    # -- Validation ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _validate_structure(self, X):
        """Validate the configured structure against the input data.

        Raises ``ValueError`` when:

        - no DGP is configured (no graph / column_mapping available);
        - the graph is not a valid DAG;
        - ``X`` has as many columns as the graph has nodes;
        - the column_mapping is a dict covering exactly the graph nodes
          with unique, in-range integer column indices.

        Returns nothing: all state needed downstream lives on ``self``
        (``self.graph``, ``self.column_mapping``).
        """
        graph = self.graph
        column_mapping = self.column_mapping
        if graph is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "no DGP configured: pass a dgp=... to the constructor, "
                "or use use_dgp(dgp) (the DGP carries graph and "
                "column_mapping)"
            )
        validate_dag(graph)
        n_features = X.shape[1]
        if n_features != len(graph.nodes):
            raise ValueError(
                f"X has {n_features} columns but graph has "
                f"{len(graph.nodes)} nodes"
            )
        if column_mapping is None:
            raise ValueError("column_mapping parameter is required")
        if not isinstance(column_mapping, dict):
            raise ValueError(
                "column_mapping must be a dict, "
                f"got {type(column_mapping).__name__}"
            )
        for node in graph.nodes:
            if not isinstance(node, str):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"graph nodes must be strings, "
                    f"got {type(node).__name__} for node '{node}'"
                )
        missing = set(graph.nodes) - set(column_mapping.keys())
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"column_mapping missing node(s): {sorted(missing)}"
            )
        extra = set(column_mapping.keys()) - set(graph.nodes)
        if extra:
            raise ValueError(
                f"column_mapping has unknown node(s): {sorted(extra)}"
            )
        seen = {}
        for node, idx in column_mapping.items():
            if not isinstance(idx, int):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"column_mapping values must be int, "
                    f"got {type(idx).__name__} for node '{node}'"
                )
            if idx < 0 or idx >= n_features:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"column index {idx} for node '{node}' "
                    f"is out of range [0, {n_features - 1}]"
                )
            if idx in seen:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"duplicate column index {idx} "
                    f"for nodes {sorted([seen[idx], node])}"
                )
            seen[idx] = node

    def _validate_perturbation_nodes(self, perturbation_nodes):
        """Validate the perturbation nodes against the configured graph.

        Requires a non-empty list of nodes that exist in the graph.
        Raises ``ValueError`` otherwise; returns nothing.

        Only the legacy ``quantile_range`` fallback of
        ``CausalImbalanceGenerator`` still takes node names.
        """
        graph = self.graph
        if graph is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "no DGP configured: pass a dgp=... to the constructor, "
                "or use use_dgp(dgp) (the DGP carries graph and "
                "column_mapping)"
            )
        if perturbation_nodes is None:
            raise ValueError("perturbation_nodes parameter is required")
        if not isinstance(perturbation_nodes, list):
            raise ValueError(
                "perturbation_nodes must be a list, "
                f"got {type(perturbation_nodes).__name__}"
            )
        if len(perturbation_nodes) == 0:
            raise ValueError("perturbation_nodes must not be empty")
        for node in perturbation_nodes:
            if node not in graph.nodes:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"perturbation node '{node}' not found in graph"
                )

    def _node_names(self, columns):
        """Node names for column positions (inverse of ``column_mapping``).

        Total after :meth:`_validate_structure`: the mapping is a bijection
        between graph nodes and in-range column indices, so every valid
        position has exactly one name.
        """
        names = {col: node for node, col in self.column_mapping.items()}
        return [names[c] for c in columns]
