import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import networkx as nx
import numpy as np
"""Shared helpers for the tabular-data tutorials. Imported by the notebooks in this directory via ``from _shared import ...``. Kept as a plain module (leading underscore) so it stays out of the docs build. """ import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import networkx as nx import numpy as np In [ ]: Copied! 
def generate_linear_data(graph, n_samples=100, rng=None, coefficients=None):
    """Generate data from a linear structural equation model on a DAG.

    Each edge (u -> v) carries a coefficient w. Every node value is
        v = sum_{u in parents(v)} w_{u,v} * u + noise
    with noise ~ N(0, 1).
    """
    if rng is None:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
    if coefficients is None:
        coefficients = {edge: 1.0 for edge in graph.edges()}

    nodes = list(graph.nodes())
    node_to_idx = {node: i for i, node in enumerate(nodes)}
    X = np.zeros((n_samples, len(nodes)))
    for node in nx.topological_sort(graph):
        idx = node_to_idx[node]
        parents = list(graph.predecessors(node))
        if not parents:
            X[:, idx] = rng.normal(size=n_samples)
        else:
            X[:, idx] = rng.normal(size=n_samples)
            for parent in parents:
                coef = coefficients.get((parent, node), 1.0)
                X[:, idx] += coef * X[:, node_to_idx[parent]]
    return X, {node: i for i, node in enumerate(nodes)}
def generate_linear_data(graph, n_samples=100, rng=None, coefficients=None): """Generate data from a linear structural equation model on a DAG. Each edge (u -> v) carries a coefficient w. Every node value is v = sum_{u in parents(v)} w_{u,v} * u + noise with noise ~ N(0, 1). """ if rng is None: rng = np.random.default_rng(42) if coefficients is None: coefficients = {edge: 1.0 for edge in graph.edges()} nodes = list(graph.nodes()) node_to_idx = {node: i for i, node in enumerate(nodes)} X = np.zeros((n_samples, len(nodes))) for node in nx.topological_sort(graph): idx = node_to_idx[node] parents = list(graph.predecessors(node)) if not parents: X[:, idx] = rng.normal(size=n_samples) else: X[:, idx] = rng.normal(size=n_samples) for parent in parents: coef = coefficients.get((parent, node), 1.0) X[:, idx] += coef * X[:, node_to_idx[parent]] return X, {node: i for i, node in enumerate(nodes)} In [ ]: Copied! 
def draw_graph(graph, title=None):
    """Draw a DAG with fixed left-to-right node positions.

    Nodes are placed in topological generations: roots at x = 0, their
    descendants at x = 1, and so on; siblings are stacked vertically.
    This keeps the visual layout deterministic and consistent across
    all notebooks (no force-directed layout).
    """
    generations = {}  # node -> column index
    for node in nx.topological_sort(graph):
        parents = list(graph.predecessors(node))
        generations[node] = 0 if not parents else max(generations[p] for p in parents) + 1
    columns = {}
    pos = {}
    for node, col in generations.items():
        pos[node] = (col, columns.setdefault(col, 0))
        columns[col] += 1
    # center each column vertically
    height = max(columns.values())
    pos = {node: (x, y - (columns[x] - 1) / 2) for node, (x, y) in pos.items()}
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, figsize=(6, 2))
    nx.draw(graph, pos, ax=ax, node_color="lightblue", node_size=800, arrowsize=15)
    nx.draw_networkx_labels(graph, pos, ax=ax)
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=12)
    ax.axis("off")
    return fig

def plot_missing(X, cls, Xt):
    """Scatter plots of the original and the transformed data (missing rows marked)."""
    missing_mask = np.isnan(Xt).any(axis=1)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, sharex=True, sharey=True, figsize=(8, 4))
    for label in np.unique(cls):
        ix = np.where(cls == label)
        axes[0].scatter(X[ix, 0], X[ix, 1], c=f"C{label}", label=f"{label}")
        ix = np.where(cls[~missing_mask] == label)
        axes[1].scatter(Xt[~missing_mask][ix, 0], Xt[~missing_mask][ix, 1], c=f"C{label}", label=f"{label}")
    # plot missing values
    axes[1].scatter(X[missing_mask][:, 0], X[missing_mask][:, 1], marker="x", color="black", label="missing")
    axes[0].set_title("Original")
    axes[1].set_title("Transformed")
    axes[0].legend()
    axes[1].legend()
    return fig, axes

Generate patterns with constant slope (randomly spaced)¶
Behind the scene: functions to manipulate patterns¶
Resampling a pattern¶
docs.text: The Pattern class provides a method for resampling a pattern. It is based on Cubic Spline Interpolation

docs.title: Add a linear trend to the pattern¶
docs.text: The function add_linear_trend takes three arguments: the values to be transformed, a start_value (were the new pattern should start) and end_value (where the new pattern should end)

docs.title: Add an offset (bias) to the pattern¶
docs.text: The function add_offset takes two arguments: the values to be transformed and an offset (float or int)

docs.title: Takeaways¶
docs.text:
• Patterns repeat a short random sequence at several time positions.
  • The rest of the series keeps its original behavior.

docs.title: Generate "transmission errors" in time series¶
docs.text: These are errors that affect the time index, for example: repeating values x(t) several times, dropping value x(t), or switching x(t) with x(t+1), etc.

docs.title: Goal¶
docs.text: Simulate channel errors: repeated samples (stuck transmission) and dropped samples (lost packets).

docs.title: Generating random switches in time¶
docs.text: Where x(t) and x(t+1) are switched

docs.title: Randomly repeating values (equivalent to delays)¶
docs.text: Where x(t) is repeated several times

docs.title: Repeating values in certain regions of time (time intervals)¶
Randomly dropping values¶
docs.text: This is different from missingness: with missingness the time index is not affected, only the values become NaN.

docs.title: Dropping values in certain regions of time (certain time intervals)¶
Takeaways¶
docs.text:
• Repeats lengthen the series (len(Xt) == len(X) + sum(gen.repeats_)).
  • Drops shorten it (len(Xt) == len(X) - len(gen.drops_indices_)).
  • Unlike missingness, transmission errors change the time index itself.

def make_data(n_samples=400):
    '''
    Corner blobs whose per-class scatter is elongated along the main diagonal.
    '''
    n_per_blob = n_samples // 4
    centers = [(-1, -1), (1, -1), (-1, 1), (1, 1)]
    rotation = np.array([[np.cos(np.pi / 4), -np.sin(np.pi / 4)],
                         [np.sin(np.pi / 4), np.cos(np.pi / 4)]])
    scales = np.array([0.5, 0.2])
    rng = default_rng(SEED)
    X = np.vstack([np.asarray(c) + (rng.normal(size=(n_per_blob, 2)) * scales) @ rotation.T
                   for c in centers])
    y = np.repeat(np.arange(4), n_per_blob)
    X = np.hstack([X, y.astype(float).reshape(-1, 1)])
    return X, y

    if sc.observed is None:

def sc_baseline(X, y, sc, dgp):
    return X.copy()

def sc_drift_direct(X, y, sc, dgp):
    gen = FixedShiftClassesGenerator(random_generator=default_rng(0))
    return gen.generate(
        X.copy(),
        selector=ClassSelector([0], class_column=2,
                               proportions={1: (y == 1).mean()},
                               rng=default_rng(0)),
        shift={1: (1.0, 0.0)}, variables=[0, 1])

def sc_noise_direct(X, y, sc, dgp):
    rng = default_rng(42)
    gen = AdditiveNoiseGenerator(random_generator=rng)
    noisy = get_selected_fields(
        X,
        ClassSelector([0], class_column=2,
                      proportions={1: (y == 1).mean()}, rng=rng),
        rng,
    )[:, 0]
    return gen.generate(
        X.copy(), distribution=norm(loc=0, scale=0.5), noise_std=1.0,
        selector=_FrozenSpec(noisy))

    gen = OutlierSamplingGenerator(random_generator=default_rng(0))

        X.copy(),
        selector=CountSelector([0], count=20, rng=default_rng(0)),
        out_of_distribution_sampler=JointHistogramSampler(
            bins=10, threshold_low_density=0.25),
    )
    sc.observed = ~gen.get_outliers_labels().astype(bool)
    return Xt

def apply_predictors(Xt, y_al, observed, predictors):
    """Apply the three frozen predictors to one generated test set.

    Returns an inspectable DataFrame with the observed (x, y, cls) values
    and all three frozen predictors' outputs.

    df = pd.DataFrame(Xt[:, :2], columns=["x", "y"])
    df["cls"] = np.asarray(y_al).astype(int)
    df["prediction_clf"] = predictors["clf"].predict(Xt[:, [0, 1]])
    df["prediction_reg"] = predictors["reg"].predict(Xt[:, [0, 2]])
    df["prediction_det"] = predictors["det"].predict(Xt[:, [0, 1]])
    if observed is not None:
        df["outlier"] = ~np.asarray(observed, dtype=bool)
    return df

def darken(color, f=0.45):
    """Blend a class color toward black (f = fraction of brightness kept)."""
    color = color.lstrip("#")
    r, g, b = (int(color[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))
    return "#{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}".format(round(r * f), round(g * f), round(b * f))


def wrong_clf(df):
    """Rows the frozen classifier assigns to another class than the true one."""
    return df["prediction_clf"].to_numpy() != df["cls"].to_numpy()


def wrong_reg(df):
    """Rows whose continuous y prediction misses the observed y by > 0.5."""
    return np.abs(df["prediction_reg"].to_numpy() - df["y"].to_numpy()) > 0.5


def overlay(ax, X2, y_true, observed=None, wrong=None, ms=POINT_MS, alpha=1.0):
    """Rows in their true class color (white rims); rows in `wrong` darker."""
    if wrong is None:
        scatter_classes(ax, X2, y_true, observed=observed, ms=ms,
                        edgecolor="white", mew=POINT_EDGE, alpha=alpha)
    else:
        obs = np.ones(len(X2), dtype=bool) if observed is None else observed
        scatter_classes(ax, X2, y_true, observed=obs & ~wrong, ms=ms,
                        edgecolor="white", mew=POINT_EDGE, alpha=alpha)
        scatter_classes(ax, X2, y_true, observed=obs & wrong, ms=ms,
                        edgecolor="white", mew=POINT_EDGE, color_fn=darken, alpha=alpha)
    if observed is not None:
        outlier_marks(ax, X2, y_true, ~observed, wrong=wrong,
                      ms=OUTLIER_MS,
                      markeredgewidth=OUTLIER_EDGE,

def boundary_legend(fig, pad_pt=1):  # 1.44 pt = 2 px at 100 dpi
    """Two stacked figure legends: classes on line 1, wrong/outliers below.

    constrained layout reserves a single outside band per side, so two
    legends sharing one "outside" loc overlap. Instead, each legend gets
    an explicit bbox: row 1 anchored to the figure top-left, row 2 just
    below row 1's measured extent, and the layout rect shrunk so the
    axes clear both rows.
    """
    outlier_handle = Line2D([], [], marker="x", markersize=3.5, color="0.35",
                            linestyle="none", label="outliers")
    common = dict(fontsize=8, frameon=False, handlelength=1.4,
                  handletextpad=0.4, columnspacing=1.2)
    pad_px = pad_pt * fig.dpi / 72
    row1 = fig.legend(handles=[*CLASS_HANDLES], loc="upper left",
                      bbox_to_anchor=(0, 1), bbox_transform=fig.transFigure,
                      ncols=4, **common)
    fig.canvas.draw()
    renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
    to_frac = fig.transFigure.inverted()
    below_row1 = row1.get_window_extent(renderer).transformed(to_frac).y0
    row2 = fig.legend(handles=[WRONG_HANDLE, outlier_handle], loc="upper left",
                      bbox_to_anchor=(0, 0.95),
                      bbox_transform=fig.transFigure, ncols=2, **common)
    fig.canvas.draw()
    occupied = (row1.get_window_extent(renderer).height
                + row2.get_window_extent(renderer).height
                + 3 * pad_px) / fig.bbox.height
    fig.get_layout_engine().set(rect=(0, 0, 1, 1 - occupied))





def plot_classifier(ax, predictions, grid, rgba):
    """Draw the classifier map and its case observations on an Axes."""
    extent = (grid.xx0.min(), grid.xx0.max(),
              grid.xx1.min(), grid.xx1.max())
    ax.imshow(rgba, origin="lower", extent=extent, aspect="auto",
              interpolation="nearest")
    ax.set_xlim(extent[0], extent[1])
    ax.set_ylim(extent[2], extent[3])
    X2 = predictions[["x", "y"]].to_numpy()
    y_true = predictions["cls"].to_numpy()
    observed = (None if "outlier" not in predictions
                else ~predictions["outlier"].to_numpy())
    overlay(ax, X2, y_true, observed, wrong=wrong_clf(predictions))
    return ax


def plot_detector(ax, predictions, grid):
    """Draw the detector score map and its case observations on an Axes."""
    ax.contourf(grid.xx0, grid.xx1, -grid.response, cmap="PRGn",
                levels=21, vmin=-0.35, vmax=0.35, extend="both", alpha=0.5)
    ax.contour(grid.xx0, grid.xx1, -grid.response, levels=[0.0],
               colors="0.15", linewidths=1.0)
    ax.set_xlim(grid.xx0.min(), grid.xx0.max())
    ax.set_ylim(grid.xx1.min(), grid.xx1.max())
    X2 = predictions[["x", "y"]].to_numpy()
    y_true = predictions["cls"].to_numpy()
    observed = (None if "outlier" not in predictions
                else ~predictions["outlier"].to_numpy())
    overlay(ax, X2, y_true, observed)
    return ax


def plot_regression(ax, predictions, regressor, x_grid):
    """Draw class-conditioned regression curves and observations on an Axes."""
    wrong = wrong_reg(predictions)
    appended = (predictions["outlier"].to_numpy() if "outlier" in predictions
                else np.zeros(len(predictions), dtype=bool))
    y_classes = predictions["cls"].to_numpy()
    for cls, color in enumerate(CLASS_COLORS):
        model_input = np.column_stack([x_grid, np.full(len(x_grid), cls)])
        y_grid = regressor.predict(model_input)
        ax.step(x_grid, y_grid, where="post", color=color,
                linewidth=0.9, linestyle='-', zorder=4)
        selected = y_classes == cls
        overlay(ax, predictions.loc[selected, ["x", "y"]].to_numpy(),
                y_classes[selected], observed=~appended[selected],
                wrong=wrong[selected], alpha=0.5)
    return ax

Instead, each legend gets an explicit bbox: row 1 anchored to the figure top-left, row 2 just below row 1's measured extent, and the layout rect shrunk so the axes clear both rows. """ outlier_handle = Line2D([], [], marker="x", markersize=3.5, color="0.35", linestyle="none", label="outliers") common = dict(fontsize=8, frameon=False, handlelength=1.4, handletextpad=0.4, columnspacing=1.2) pad_px = pad_pt * fig.dpi / 72 row1 = fig.legend(handles=[*CLASS_HANDLES], loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0, 1), bbox_transform=fig.transFigure, ncols=4, **common) fig.canvas.draw() renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer() to_frac = fig.transFigure.inverted() below_row1 = row1.get_window_extent(renderer).transformed(to_frac).y0 row2 = fig.legend(handles=[WRONG_HANDLE, outlier_handle], loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0, 0.95), bbox_transform=fig.transFigure, ncols=2, **common) fig.canvas.draw() occupied = (row1.get_window_extent(renderer).height + row2.get_window_extent(renderer).height + 3 * pad_px) / fig.bbox.height fig.get_layout_engine().set(rect=(0, 0, 1, 1 - occupied)) def plot_classifier(ax, predictions, grid, rgba): """Draw the classifier map and its case observations on an Axes.""" extent = (grid.xx0.min(), grid.xx0.max(), grid.xx1.min(), grid.xx1.max()) ax.imshow(rgba, origin="lower", extent=extent, aspect="auto", interpolation="nearest") ax.set_xlim(extent[0], extent[1]) ax.set_ylim(extent[2], extent[3]) X2 = predictions[["x", "y"]].to_numpy() y_true = predictions["cls"].to_numpy() observed = (None if "outlier" not in predictions else ~predictions["outlier"].to_numpy()) overlay(ax, X2, y_true, observed, wrong=wrong_clf(predictions)) return ax def plot_detector(ax, predictions, grid): """Draw the detector score map and its case observations on an Axes.""" ax.contourf(grid.xx0, grid.xx1, -grid.response, cmap="PRGn", levels=21, vmin=-0.35, vmax=0.35, extend="both", alpha=0.5) ax.contour(grid.xx0, grid.xx1, -grid.response, levels=[0.0], colors="0.15", linewidths=1.0) ax.set_xlim(grid.xx0.min(), grid.xx0.max()) ax.set_ylim(grid.xx1.min(), grid.xx1.max()) X2 = predictions[["x", "y"]].to_numpy() y_true = predictions["cls"].to_numpy() observed = (None if "outlier" not in predictions else ~predictions["outlier"].to_numpy()) overlay(ax, X2, y_true, observed) return ax def plot_regression(ax, predictions, regressor, x_grid): """Draw class-conditioned regression curves and observations on an Axes.""" wrong = wrong_reg(predictions) appended = (predictions["outlier"].to_numpy() if "outlier" in predictions else np.zeros(len(predictions), dtype=bool)) y_classes = predictions["cls"].to_numpy() for cls, color in enumerate(CLASS_COLORS): model_input = np.column_stack([x_grid, np.full(len(x_grid), cls)]) y_grid = regressor.predict(model_input) ax.step(x_grid, y_grid, where="post", color=color, linewidth=0.9, linestyle='-', zorder=4) selected = y_classes == cls overlay(ax, predictions.loc[selected, ["x", "y"]].to_numpy(), y_classes[selected], observed=~appended[selected], wrong=wrong[selected], alpha=0.5) return ax In [21]: Copied!

docs.title: Illustrating Badgers for testing ML predictors¶
docs.text:
End-to-end walk-through of the paper experiment, step by step:

  1. Data — make_data(): four corner blobs with columns (x, y, cls)
  2. Split — stratified 50/50 train/test (split_data)
  3. Direct (non-causal) deficits — generators applied to the test half: drift, noise, outliers
  4. Causal deficits — the same deficits injected through the SCM fitted on the train half (build_dgp), so a \(do\)-intervention on \(x\) propagates to \(y\)
  5. Predictors + impact table — RandomForestClassifier / RandomForestRegressor / IsolationForest fitted once on the clean train half, evaluated on every deficit variant
  6. Decision maps and regression curves — frozen classifier and detector maps over clean/direct/causal data, plus class-conditioned Random Forest regression curves for predicting \(y\) from \((x, cls)\)

Requires the badgers package and the causal generators' optional dowhy extra (pip install badgers[dowhy]).

docs.title: 1. Data generation — four diagonal corner blobs¶
docs.text:
• make_data builds four Gaussian blobs at the corners \((\pm1, \pm1)\) — 400 points total. One seed (SEED = 42) drives a single RNG stream that draws, blob by blob, isotropic noise scaled by the vector \(\mathrm{scales} = (0.5, 0.2)\) and then rotated by \(45°\) via the matrix \(R\). Each blob is elongated along the main diagonal.

  • align_y rebuilds the ground-truth labels for the generated set. The in-place generators return the same 200 rows with the original labels; the outlier generators append 20 rows that are copies of seed rows, so their class is read from the untouched cls cell of the generated matrix (Xt[len(y):, 2]).

docs.title: Generatring the data¶
docs.text: Four Gaussian blobs at the corners \((\pm1, \pm1)\), elongated along the main diagonal (scales \(0.5 \times 0.2\), rotated \(45°\)). X has three columns \((x, y, \mathrm{cls})\); y is the class index \(0..3\).

docs.title: Fitting the causal data-generating process (SCM)¶
docs.text:
build_dgp wraps a structural causal model (SCM) in a badgers GcmSCMDGP so the causal generators can inject defects and propagate them through the learned mechanism.

The graph encodes:

  • \(\mathrm{cls} \to x\),
  • \(\mathrm{cls} \to y\)
  • \(x \to y\)

root "cls" gets EmpiricalDistribution — it just resamples observed class values.

"x" gets an AdditiveNoiseModel whose prediction model is a pipeline OneHotEncoder → LinearRegression — i.e. the learned conditional mean \(\mathbb{E}[x \mid \mathrm{cls}]\) (one mean per blob) plus the fitted noise term, so \(x = f_x(\mathrm{cls}) + N_x\).

"y" gets an AdditiveNoiseModel over the feature block OneHotEncoder(cls) ⊕ passthrough(x) followed by a linear regression — i.e. \(y = f_y(\mathrm{cls}, x) + N_y\), capturing both the class offset and the diagonal tilt. This is the edge that makes a \(do\)-intervention on \(x\) propagate to \(y\).

GcmSCMDGP(scm, COLUMN_MAPPING).fit(X) maps the column names to positions (x → 0, y → 1, cls → 2) and fits all noise models on the clean train half; the resulting dgp object is what the causal generators in section 4 consume. Needs the optional dowhy extra.

docs.title: 2. Applying the generators¶
docs.text:
Every deficit below is run as a scenario: a name, a family tag (direct / causal / reference), and the generated test set. Two pieces of glue are needed around the generators:

  • Scenario is a small state holder; sc.observed records, as a boolean mask aligned with the generated output, which rows are original rows (True) and which are appended outlier rows (False). In-place generators (drift, noise) leave it None — all rows are original.
  • _FrozenSpec is an adapter for the noise generator: instead of a selector object it hands over an already-computed boolean spec of which cells to corrupt, so the noise lands exactly on the cells selected upstream (figure bookkeeping, kept for reproducibility with the paper contract).

docs.title: The six deficit scenarios¶
docs.text:
Three deficits × two injection layers (plus the untouched baseline), each a function fn(X, y, sc, dgp) -> Xt that applies the exact generators of the paper figures to the test data:

  • direct drift — FixedShiftClassesGenerator moves the class-1 rows by the absolute vector shift={1: (1.0, 0.0)} on the columns variables=[0, 1] (so \(x \leftarrow x+1\), \(y \leftarrow y\), no propagation); ClassSelector picks the affected rows in class-1 proportion.
  • direct noise — AdditiveNoiseGenerator adds \(\mathcal{N}(0, 0.5^2)\) (scale × noise_std=1.0) to the class-1 x cells; the cells are selected up front and passed through _FrozenSpec.
  • direct outliers — OutlierSamplingGenerator appends count=20 rows drawn from JointHistogramSampler's low-density bins — regions where the seed data has almost no support. sc.observed records the 200 original vs 20 appended rows (~gen.get_outliers_labels()).
  • causal variants — the same three deficits, but as \(do\)-interventions routed through the fitted SCM (dgp=dgp): CausalDriftGenerator shifts \(x\) by shift_amount * std(x), CausalNoiseGenerator adds relative noise noise_std=0.5, and CausalOutlierPropagationGenerator replaces \(x\) of the 20 seed rows with OOD values and re-samples their descendants (\(y\)) through the SCM. Each causal call re-derives the class-proportion selector, so both layers hit the same rows.

SCENARIOS lists them in the order the impact table consumes; each entry is instantiated into a fresh Scenario at run time so per-run state (observed) never leaks between evaluations.

docs.title: Applying direct (non-causal) generators on the test data¶
Visualizing the generated test data¶
docs.text: The clean test half (a) next to the three generated variants — the 2x2 grid makes every change directly comparable against the original data.

docs.title: Applying causal generators on the test data¶
docs.text: The same three deficits, but injected through the SCM \(\mathrm{cls} \to x\), \(\mathrm{cls} \to y\), \(x \to y\) fitted on the train half (build_dgp), so a \(do\)-intervention on \(x\) propagates to \(y\) as well.

docs.title: 3. Training the predictors¶
docs.text:
train_predictors fits the three downstream predictors once, on the clean train half, and returns them (all with random_state=SEED so the whole notebook is reproducible):

  • clf — RandomForestClassifier, features \((x, y)\) → class index (the cls column cast back to int)
  • reg — RandomForestRegressor, features \(x,c\) → x (treating the class index as a continuous blob coordinate)
  • det — IsolationForest, unsupervised on \((x, y)\) only, with contamination=0.1 to match the expected outlier rate

docs.title: 4. Measuring how predictors react to the deficits¶
docs.text: All three predictors are fitted once on the clean train half and then frozen. Each table row evaluates them on one deficit variant of the test half (evaluate, labels aligned via align_y: appended outlier rows keep their seed row's class, read from the untouched cls cell). Columns: classifier accuracy and macro \(F_1\); regressor MSE and \(R^2\) for the continuous \(y\) target; detector mean anomaly score (higher = more normal), share flagged by IsolationForest (contamination \(= 0.1\)), and share scoring above the clean test half's 90th-percentile anomaly score \(p_{90}\).

docs.title: Evaluation helpers¶
docs.text:
Two helpers make the generated outputs comparable to the clean test half:

  • evaluate scores the three frozen predictors on the generated set Xt = (x, y, cls): classifier accuracy and macro \(F_1\); regressor MSE and \(R^2\) for continuous \(y\); detector mean anomaly score (higher = more normal), share flagged by IsolationForest.predict() == -1, and share scoring above the clean test half's 90th-percentile anomaly score p90_clean. It returns a flat metric dict for the impact table plus an extra dict covering the appended rows only (share flagged / above \(p_{90}\) among the outliers themselves).

docs.title: Applying the predictors to the transformed data¶
docs.text:
Idea. The three frozen predictors are applied once to every transformed test set — the clean test half and the six deficit variants of the two preceding sections (the same rows that were saved under generated-data/) — and the predictions are kept in one inspectable data structure: PREDICTIONS maps a case name to a DataFrame with one row per generated row:

  • x, y — observed feature x and continuous regression target y,
  • cls — the true class (aligned via align_y) and the regressor's second input,
  • prediction_clf — the classifier's predicted class index,
  • prediction_reg — the regressor's predicted continuous y value,
  • prediction_det — the detector's prediction (-1 means flagged),
  • outlier — True for the appended outlier rows (outlier cases only).

Everything below only reads PREDICTIONS — no predictor is called while drawing.

docs.title: 5. Visualizing predictors decisions boundaries and regression lines¶
docs.text: Idea. The decision functions are frozen — fitted once on the clean train half — so their boundary images are computed once on dense \(400 \times 400\) grids and reused in the classifier and detector maps below. The classifier colors each grid cell with the winning class, faded toward white by the vote margin (\(\sqrt{\max p}\)). Regression is shown separately as class-conditioned step curves: the model input is \((x, cls)\) and its continuous output is \(y\).

docs.title: Drawing helpers¶
docs.text: Idea. All per-point drawing reads the stored predictions, never the predictors. A row is drawn in a darker shade of its class color when the panel's predictor handles it wrong — wrong_clf flags rows whose predicted class differs from the true one. wrong_reg marks rows whose continuous prediction differs from the observed \(y\) by more than \(0.5\) target units. overlay draws rows class by class with white rims and stamps appended outliers with class-colored \(\times\) marks.
